spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the spec's literal definition ('If the side attribute is right, then reverse path') by carrying a real path-data reverser and measuring whether side="right" produces the same first-glyph geometry as the reversed data.

interactive.rationale: The reverse button genuinely rewrites panel B's d attribute (works in every browser, including the unsupported build environment), redraws direction arrows from getPointAtLength, and re-measures all three panels.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises computed direction arrows and a working reverser measured against side="right"; the page does both.

edge_cases.rationale: The reverser explicitly throws on relative commands and Z (documented limitation matching the open single-subpath demo path), the comparison handles unmeasurable text, and the supported/unsupported/reversed states each have distinct honest readouts.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5422782593761280 and the spec's TextPathElementSideAttribute anchor.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's side-right-reverses-open-path assertion is the same measured contract this page demonstrates interactively; the reverser is the everywhere-available control arm.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Verified headless (Chromium 141): clicking the button moved panel B's text 354.9px (measured), arrows turned around, panel A stayed on the reference, console clean; screenshots read at both device classes before and after interaction.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts manual-path-reversal-flips-text (>100px measured movement) on the interaction that works everywhere, plus the supported/fallback probe asserts on load.

design_system.rationale: Arrows, start dots, paths, and text are all styled through classes bound to CSS variables; the toggled button state overrides background and colour together.

accessibility.rationale: The reverse control is a real button with aria-pressed and a text label that changes with state, SVGs have role=img plus desc, the d-string output is selectable text, and the comparison summary is one polite live region.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Three panels collapse to one column via auto-fit minmax(min(100%, 260px), 1fr), the long d-string wraps with overflow-wrap anywhere, no horizontal overflow at 360px; verified at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800.

openQuestions.title: Verify A-equals-B convergence on a Chrome 156 build
openQuestions.detail: On a supporting browser, after pressing the reverse button, panels A and B should measure within ~1px of each other (the readout has a dedicated branch for a partial mismatch). Confirm that branch reports equality on Chrome 156 and consider tightening the message if sub-pixel differences appear.

guidanceConsulted.query: toggle button state accessible name aria-pressed
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use a native button for toggles, expose state via aria-pressed, and keep the visible label in sync with state; keep focus visible.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The reverse control is a native button with aria-pressed true/false, a label that flips between reverse/restore, a pressed background+colour pair, and a :focus-visible outline.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel without horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: auto-fit minmax with a min(100%) guard for card grids; overflow-wrap for long unbroken strings instead of letting them force page width.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Panel grid uses minmax(min(100%, 260px), 1fr); the generated d-string output uses overflow-wrap: anywhere so reversed path data never widens the page.

summary: The inspection/comparison angle: direction arrows computed from live path geometry, a real M/L/Q/C/A path-data reverser behind a toggle button that works in every browser today, and a three-way measured comparison showing that side="right" is (where supported) geometrically identical to the hand-reversed data — and honestly showing it doing nothing on the Chromium 141 build environment.
